html:
The Huarpe are an Indigenous people of the Cuyo region of western Argentina, in today's Mendoza, San Juan and San Luis provinces. They lived in the dry valleys at the foot of the Andes, farming maize, beans and squash with irrigation, and fishing in the lagoons of Guanacache.

In the late 1400s the Inca Empire extended its rule south into Cuyo, and its roads and irrigation works reached the Mendoza valley.

Spaniards from Chile crossed the Andes and founded Mendoza in 1561 and San Juan in 1562. Under the encomienda system many Huarpe were marched over the mountains to work in Chile, and their numbers fell sharply. By the 1700s the Huarpe had largely lost their language. In recent decades Huarpe communities around Guanacache have organised again and won back some land. Neighbours: Diaguita and Rankülche.
